findings.title: Upright phone settings hide the Audio and Accessibility tabs off-screen with no sign that more tabs exist
findings.detail: A player holding the phone upright sees four tabs that end cleanly at the right margin and nothing that says the strip scrolls. Anyone looking for Audio or Accessibility, the players who most need to find it, has no cue that those pages exist. Landscape (settings@phone) at least shows a clipped 'ACCESSIB' as a hint; upright shows none.
findings.fix: On upright phones wrap the tabs onto two rows, or keep the sideways scroll but always leave half a tab cut at the right edge plus a fade or chevron so the strip reads as scrollable.
findings.evidence: settings@phone-upright controls: TOUCH [16,87,65,44], CONTROLS [83,87,92,44], VIDEO [312,87,61,44] ends at x=373; AUDIO starts at [375,87,62,44], past the 374 px content edge of a 390 px viewport. settings-hud@phone-upright has ACCESSIBILITY at [376,87,121,44], also fully outside. settings@phone shows the clipped tab at [751,10,125,44].

findings.title: The match result headline ('Defeat', 'Orange wins') floats on the sky with no plate
findings.detail: The one line that tells the player whether they won is the only text on the end screen without a surface behind it. Grey 'Defeat' over a pale sky is the weakest; the orange team line survives on its size and shadow. The same headline on end-panel@phone measures lower still, and end-vote@desktop shows a grey 'Victory' over cloud.
findings.fix: Move the result headline into the top of the end panel, or give it its own ink plate or a top-edge scrim like the bottom one used for the HUD.
findings.evidence: contrast.md, end-vote@phone: 'Defeat' 22 px bold declared 9.47, measured p50 1.5 / p10 1.46; '▲ Orange wins' 32 px bold declared 8.74, measured p50 1.47 / p10 1.23 (large text needs 3). end-panel@phone: 1.22 and 1.15. Every line inside the panel below passes. · 'Defeat' [250,14,64,22] 22 px, colour rgb(180,186,197): contrast 1.5 / 1.46. '▲ Orange wins' [327,6,267,32] 32 px team orange: 1.47 / 1.23 (needs 3). 'Back to the lobby in 0:05' [351,215,141,13] 13 px. · end-vote@phone (after the flash): "Defeat" 22 px bold #b4bac5 measures 1.50:1 (p10 1.46), "Orange wins" 32 px 1.47:1 (p10 1.23); need 3:1. countdown@desktop: "Team deathmatch" 16 px 1.81:1, the countdown number 2.03:1. · end-vote@phone: "Defeat" 22 px, rgb(180,186,197), p50 1.5 / p10 1.46 (needs 3); "▲ Orange wins" 32 px, p50 1.47 / p10 1.23 (needs 3). countdown@desktop: "Team deathmatch" 16 px p50 1.81 (needs 4.5), the number "2" p50 2.03 (needs 3). countdown@phone: 3.9 / 1.79 and 3.34 / 2.82.
alsoNoted: hierarchy: The match result is unplated over bright sky, and the player's own outcome is the faintest word on the screen
hud: The verdict ("Defeat", "Orange wins") is set straight on the sky with only a shadow
rules: The match result ("Defeat", "Orange wins") is drawn on bright sky with only a shadow and measures about 1.5:1

findings.title: On a phone the destination list is shifted off the left edge and the one playable destination is cut by the fold
findings.detail: The title, name field and rank hold the 16 px gutter but the destinations start 92 px further right, so the screen has two left edges. The name and rank rows take the top third, which leaves room for only the two online destinations (both dead when no server answers); the lit choice, Bot Match, is sliced by the bottom of the screen and Practice Range and Settings are out of sight with nothing saying the list scrolls. The page title and the destinations are also 2 px apart in size.
findings.fix: Start the destination list at the gutter (x 16) and move the name field and rank to the right half beside it, as the world/readout side, so four destinations fit in 390 px with the lit one fully visible; in the short-phone header use the heading-size title DESIGN.md already asks for.
findings.evidence: Destination rows are 720 px wide at x 108 ([108,201,720,74]); title, name field and rank at x 16. 'Bot Match' title at [126,355,160,30] in a 390 px tall viewport, its readout below the fold. 'Duty Shooter' 32 px vs destinations 30 px.

findings.title: On a phone held sideways the first screen shows only the two places that need the server
findings.detail: The name field and Rank line take the top half, so only Play Online and Battle Royale fit. Bot Match, the lit row and the one that works here, is cut at its title, and Practice Range and Settings are off screen with only a thin scrollbar to say so. A first-time phone player reads 'No game server answers this page' and sees no other way to play.
findings.fix: In landscape under 520 px tall, put the name field and Rank on the title's row at the right (as on desktop) so the list starts near y 60, and tighten the rows so all four destinations show.
findings.evidence: Rank/Profile button ends at y 183 of 390; destinations start at y 201. Play Online [108,201,720,74], Battle Royale [108,275,720,74], Bot Match [108,349,720,74]: 41 of its 74 px are on screen, its readout line is not. Practice Range and Settings are absent from the visible DOM sample.

findings.title: HUD size is locked on phones, where the HUD labels are already at the 13 px floor
findings.detail: New idea: a text-size control should not be withdrawn on the device where text is physically smallest. On a phone the HUD size slider is disabled with a note that the screen keeps its own layout, so a player who finds the labels too small has no way to enlarge them. Same on settings-hud@phone-upright.
findings.fix: Keep the phone layout fixed but let the slider scale the text inside the plates and toasts (for example 100 to 130%), or offer a 'Larger HUD text' switch on phones.
findings.evidence: settings-hud@phone: 'HUD size' input [32,325,708,44] disabled, note 'A screen this narrow keeps its own layout.' [32,303,247,13]. settings-hud@phone-upright: input [32,439,254,44] disabled. match-hud@phone HUD labels 'Health' [325,332,39,13], 'auto' and '/ ∞' are 13 px; values 22 px.

findings.title: The destructive 'Reset profile' sits in the slot where every other page has its main action
findings.detail: On every other page the bottom-right corner is Start, Done or Check again, so a player's hand goes there to move on; on Profile that corner erases their progress. On profile@phone it is the wider of two buttons and sits 8 px from Back.
findings.fix: Take Reset out of the footer: put it at the end of the page body as a quiet text button with its one-line consequence, and leave the footer with Back only (or Back in the primary slot).
findings.evidence: 'RESET PROFILE' [1675,1022,189,44] at the footer's right end; primary actions elsewhere at [1604,1008,260,58]. Phone: 'RESET PROFILE' [149,338,189,44] next to 'BACK' [16,338,125,44].

findings.title: 'Passphrase' is asked for with no word on what it is or whether it is needed
findings.detail: Play Online shows two empty fields, Name and Passphrase, with no placeholder or help line. A first-time player does not know which passphrase is meant, where to get it, or whether the field can stay empty. Same on online@phone-upright; on online@phone the field is under the fold.
findings.fix: Add one line under the field: 'Only if the host set one. Leave it empty otherwise', or hide the field until the server reports that it wants a passphrase.
findings.evidence: Label 'Passphrase' 13 px at [1462,302,69,13]; input [1462,326,384,46] with an empty label and no placeholder; no other text in the 'Your details' panel.

findings.title: With the server down the primary slot holds a dead button and the one working action is a grey button at the far corner
findings.detail: The eye goes to the big bottom-right button, which reads 'Server offline' and cannot be pressed; the only thing that helps, 'Check again', is a secondary 1400 px away at the left. The same state is said three times (chip, sentence, button) while nothing dominant says what to do. Battle Royale in the same state already makes 'Check again' the primary. Same on online@phone and online@phone-upright.
findings.fix: When no server answers, make 'Check again' the .ds-btn.primary.big in the footer's primary slot as the Battle Royale screen does, keep the reason in the connection line only, and drop the chip or the disabled button so the state is said once.
findings.evidence: Disabled primary 'SERVER OFFLINE' [1604,1008,260,58]; 'CHECK AGAIN' [193,1015,171,44] secondary; chip 'Server not answering' [1662,74,189,13]; sentence at [56,293,1002,16]. royale@desktop: 'CHECK AGAIN' is the primary at [1604,1008,260,58]. · "SERVER OFFLINE" text [1653,1029,162,16] in --ds-signal on --ds-signal-dim, button [1604,1008,260,58] disabled:true; phone text [497,352,162,16]; upright [114,802,162,16]. DESIGN.md: "Don't use --ds-signal for status text that can't be acted on".
alsoNoted: rules: The disabled "Server offline" button is written in the signal colour that means "press this"

findings.title: Play Online on a sideways phone opens with focus on a Name field hidden under the footer
findings.detail: The screen takes focus into the Name text field by itself, and on a landscape phone that field sits behind the footer row, so the focused control is invisible and a keyboard may rise over the page. Only the 'Your details' heading shows above the buttons. online@phone-upright also opens with the field focused, there visible.
findings.fix: On touch do not auto-focus the Name field; focus the footer's primary action (or nothing), and make sure the body's scroll area ends above the footer so the field can be scrolled fully into view.
findings.evidence: online@phone .dom.json: focused input [34,362,776,46] in a 390 px tall viewport; footer BACK [16,338,125,44], CHECK AGAIN [149,338,171,44], SERVER OFFLINE [327,338,501,44] cover y 338 to 382. online@phone-upright: input [34,476,322,46] focused. DESIGN.md: on touch 'a text field never takes the focus by itself'.

findings.title: The name field and the connection line sit under the island picture, far from the slot that asks for the name
findings.detail: The left column's own slot says 'Type your name to join', but the field it means is a 1104 px wide input in the opposite column, below the picture and below a status line. A prompt and the control it points to should be one group (no rule covers grouping). A player reads top-left to bottom-left and finds no field there; the phone layout already puts the name first.
findings.fix: Move the name field into the 'You' slot (or directly under the squad slots in the left column) at a field's normal width, and keep the connection line with the footer action it explains.
findings.evidence: 'You' / 'Type your name to join' at [73,489]-[73,518,131,13]; 'Name' label [760,788,34,13] and input [760,812,1104,46], about 700 px to the right and 300 px lower; status line [779,736,538,16] between the picture and the field.

findings.title: With the server down, Battle Royale offers only 'Check again' and never points at Local bots
findings.detail: The status line says to try again in a minute and the primary button is Check again, yet 'Local bots' plays the whole mode offline. On a phone held sideways the 'Play on' switch is under the fold, below Name, Your Squad and Squads. On royale@desktop the switch is in view but the line beside it still only says to wait, where Play Online's own message names Bot Match as the way to play meanwhile.
findings.fix: When the server does not answer, end the status line with 'Local bots plays now, offline' and make the primary action 'Play with local bots', with Check again beside it. Put 'Play on' first in the phone's order.
findings.evidence: Visible texts in royale@phone: 'The game server isn't answering. It may be restarting: try again in a minute.' [35,80,538,16], Name, Your Squad, footer Back and 'Check again'. 'Play on' appears at y 586 in royale@phone-upright and at [56,149] on desktop, where LOCAL BOTS [317,174,259,48] is enabled.

findings.title: Touch choices are stacked 1 to 2 px apart instead of 8 px
findings.detail: Every target is at least 44 px tall, but stacked segment rows and the settings tabs touch each other, so a thumb landing on the seam picks the neighbour. In the mode picker three 44 px rows sit directly on top of one another. Same pattern on royale@phone-upright, the settings tabs on phone and phone-upright, and the pause list on pause@phone.
findings.fix: On touch give stacked segment rows and tabs an 8 px gap (or make each row 52 px tall with the hit area inset), and space the pause rows by 8 px.
findings.evidence: bot-lobby@phone-upright: TEAM DEATHMATCH [17,604,178,44], FREE-FOR-ALL [196,604,178,44], OUTPOSTS [17,649,178,44], CHARGE [196,649,178,44], GUN GAME [17,694,356,44]: 1 px between rows and columns. royale@phone-upright: SOLOS/DUOS/TRIOS at x 17/136/255, width 118: 1 px. settings@phone tabs TOUCH [136,10,69,44] | CONTROLS [207,10,96,44]: 2 px. pause@phone RESUME [16,111,812,54] | LOADOUT [16,171,812,54]: 6 px. DESIGN.md asks for 8 px or more.

findings.title: Nine invented weapon names with one word each, and the Weapon card beside them is empty
findings.detail: A new player choosing a gun sees 'Wasp 9 auto', 'Bulwark 5.56 auto', 'M4A1 auto' and cannot tell a submachine gun from a machine gun or a rifle. The 'Weapon' column that should describe the equipped gun is a heading with nothing under it when the screen opens. On the phone shots no description is in view either.
findings.fix: Fill the card with the equipped primary as soon as the screen opens (role sentence and bars), and replace the fire-mode word on each tile with the weapon's class and mode ('SMG · auto', 'Shotgun · pump', 'Sniper · scoped').
findings.evidence: DOM sample: each tile is a 16 px name plus a 13 px fire-mode word (auto, pump, scoped, semi, burst). The right column holds only the h2 'Weapon' at [1444,147,94,22]; no role, name or bars follow, with M4A1 equipped and Done focused.

findings.title: The countdown's mode name and number sit unplated on the sky and measure under 2:1
findings.detail: At the start of every match the mode name and the 3-2-1 number are white text straight over cloud, held up only by a shadow. The goal line right below them is on a plate and reads fine, so the two most important words of the moment are the weakest on screen. Phone has the same layout with slightly better luck in the background.
findings.fix: Extend the goal line's plate upward to hold the mode name and the number, or put a soft scrim behind the whole countdown block.
findings.evidence: contrast.md, countdown@desktop: 'Team deathmatch' 16 px bold p50 1.81 / p10 1.62 (needs 4.5); number '2' 51.84 px bold p50 2.03 / p10 1.89 (needs 3). countdown@phone: 'Team deathmatch' [359,70,126,16] 3.9 / 1.79; '2' [413,94,18,32] 3.34 / 2.82. · '2' [946,290,29,52] 51.84 px bold: contrast p50 2.03, p10 1.89 (needs 3). 'Team deathmatch' [897,267,126,16] 16 px bold: 1.81 / 1.62 (needs 4.5). Health and ammo figures are 60 px. On countdown@phone: '2' 3.34 / 2.82, 'Team deathmatch' 3.9 / 1.79.
alsoNoted: hierarchy: The opening count and the mode name are bare white text over bright sky, and the count is smaller than the health number

findings.title: Ally name tags are drawn on top of each other and on top of the Health readout
findings.detail: Two teammates held to the same screen edge get their tags at the same point, so only one name can be read and a player sees one ally where there are two; the pile sits directly above the Health label and reads as part of that block. Labels of the same kind must never stack on one another (no rule covers this). Seen too on match-hud@phone (tags read 'BriaEmber' above the crosshair), countdown@phone ('Briar' hidden under the goal-line plate) and turn-notice@phone-upright (three tags at one point).
findings.fix: Spread edge-held ally markers apart (stack them along the edge with a 4 px gap, or merge to one tag reading 'Rook, Ember'), keep them off the readout corners the way TOUCH_GROUND keeps them off the controls, and hide them under HUD plates.
findings.evidence: 'Rook' [17,940,29,13] and 'Ember' [13,940,39,13] share the same spot; only 'Ember' is readable. The 'Health' label starts at [56,964,39,13], 11 px below and 4 px right of the tag's chevron. match-hud@phone: two tags overlap at about [455,146,56,34]. · "Briar" [17,40,30,13], "Rook" [17,940,29,13], "Ember" [13,940,39,13]: x 13-17 px, safe area on 1920 px is about 57.6 px. Rook and Ember share y 940 and overlap; the Health label starts at [56,964]. turn-notice@phone-upright DOM also carries three tags at x 339-343, y 596 on one spot.
alsoNoted: rules: Ally name tags held to the screen edge sit 13-17 px from the bezel and stack on top of each other

findings.title: Desktop health and ammo readouts drop far below 4.5:1 when the ground or a wall behind them is bright
findings.detail: The corner readouts rely on a soft bottom scrim and a text shadow, so over a pale fence or sand the small labels wash out and even the big health number loses its edge. The phone layout already puts the same readouts on flat ink plates and measures above 12:1. Same on range-hud@desktop and, more mildly, match-hud@desktop.
findings.fix: Give the desktop corners the same flat ink plate the phone readouts use (or deepen the bottom scrim to at least 72% under the text block) so the p10 ratio clears 4.5:1 on any map.
findings.evidence: contrast.md, countdown@desktop: 'Health' 13 px p50 1.76 / p10 1.32; '100' 60 px bold p50 4.38 / p10 1.97 (needs 3); 'M4A1' 16 px bold 4.12 / 2.56; 'auto' 13 px 4.14 / 2.95; '/ ∞' 22 px 4.69 / 3.86. range-hud@desktop: 'auto' 3.15 / 2.39, 'M4A1' 3.49 / 2.39. match-hud@desktop p10: Health 3.43, M4A1 3.59, auto 3.53. Phone plates: Health 12.75, auto 13.68.

findings.title: The 'USE LOADOUT' prompt looks like a button and reads as an order, but the control is elsewhere
findings.detail: During the countdown a boxed line in tracked capitals, the system's button style, says 'USE LOADOUT' under the crosshair. A phone player taps it and nothing happens: the control is the round USE button 110 px to the right. On desktop the same plate reads 'F LOADOUT' with the F set as plain text, not as a keycap like WASD in the hint line, and neither version says what a loadout is.
findings.fix: Build the prompt like the hint line: the key as a keycap (or the USE glyph in its ring on touch) followed by sentence-case words that say what happens, 'Change your weapons'. On touch make the plate itself tappable.
findings.evidence: Prompt is one text run 'Use Loadout', 16 px uppercase, class ds-prompt ds-plate, box [359,233,126,16]; it is not in the controls list. The USE control is at [608,194,60,60]. countdown@desktop: 'F Loadout' one run at [910,677,101,16], no ds-kbd element, while the hint line's 'WASD' is a separate 13 px bold cap.

findings.title: Ammo, health and team scores are not in tabular figures, only the clock is
findings.detail: The magazine count is the fastest-changing number on screen and its digits have different widths, so the right-hand readout shuffles sideways as it counts down through the teens; health and the match bar's team scores do the same. DESIGN.md asks for tabular figures on all scores, timers and counts.
findings.fix: Apply `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` at the HUD root (or to .hp, .mag, .res, .score and the grenade count), and give the magazine a fixed two-digit width so the grenade count beside it never moves.
findings.evidence: DOM sample: `tabular: false` on .hp, .mag, .res, the grenade count and both .score cells on every in-play shot at both viewports; only .clock is tabular. At 60 px "100" is 85 px wide and "30" is 66 px, so a "1" takes about 19 px against 33 px for other digits. · DOM tabular:false on .hp "100" [56,982,85,60], .mag "30" [1760,982,66,60], grenade count "1" [1737,1002,5,16], both match-bar .score [860,32,12,22] / [1051,32,12,22], scoreboard td.score and td.place. Measured widths: match-bar "1" 7 px vs "0" 12 px; scoreboard "1" 5 px vs "0" 9 px, "200" 26 px vs "150" 23 px; phone magazine "30" 24 px vs "23" 23 px. Clock "9:57" is tabular:true.
alsoNoted: rules: Health, magazine, grenade count and team scores use proportional digits

findings.title: Ally markers pile onto each other, the crosshair and other HUD plates with no decluttering
findings.detail: When two teammates stand in the same direction their name plates overlap into an unreadable "BriaEmber" a few pixels off the aim point, and their chevrons sit on the crosshair's own arms. The same markers also run under or over other HUD: in score-lines@phone a chevron covers the "M" of "LONG SHOT 62 M" and two sit on the crosshair's top arm, in countdown@phone "Briar" is half buried under the goal plate, and in countdown@desktop two edge markers (Rook, Ember) collapse onto one spot right on top of the Health label so two allies read as one.
findings.fix: Add a declutter pass to ally markers: inside the centre box drop the name plate and dim the chevron; when two markers land within a plate's width, offset them vertically or merge them ("Ember +1"); draw markers under HUD plates and score lines; clamp edge markers out of the health and ammo corners as they already keep off the touch controls' ground.
findings.evidence: match-hud@phone: "Briar" and "Ember" plates overlap by about 18 px at x 456-510, y 147-163, inside the centre box (338-506 x 156-234). countdown@desktop: "Rook" [17,940,29,13] and "Ember" [13,940,39,13] share one position, 11 px above "Health" [56,964,39,13]. countdown@phone: "Briar" [291,132,30,13] under the goal plate (y 134-165).

findings.title: Eleven glyph-only touch buttons, and the hints never name Fire, Jump, Melee or Ping
findings.detail: A phone player's first spawn shows eleven round buttons with no words. The first-match hints cover the stick, aim, sprint, reload, swap, grenade, loadout and scores, so Fire, Jump, Melee and Ping are never introduced, and nothing says the gun fires by itself when the crosshair rests on an enemy (Auto-fire is on by default). Jump and Crouch are the same chevron-over-a-bar pointing up or down, Ping is a map pin that reads as 'map', and Scores is a three-line glyph beside Pause that reads as a menu.
findings.fix: Add a touch 'fire' hint right after 'move' (fire glyph + 'Rest the crosshair on an enemy and the gun fires. This button fires by hand') and one each for Jump and Ping the first time they matter. Give Jump and Crouch distinct glyphs (a standing and a crouched figure), and show a small word under each button until its hint is learned.
findings.evidence: Controls in the DOM sample: Fire 76x76, Aim 60x60, Jump, Crouch 52x52, Reload, Swap weapon, Grenade, Melee 48x48, Pause, Scoreboard, Ping 44x44; no text run belongs to any of them. HINT_IDS in hints.ts: move, aim, sprint, reload, swap, grenade, loadout, scoreboard. settings-touch: 'Auto-fire (fires when the crosshair rests on an enemy)' ON.

findings.title: The first-spawn hint on a phone is printed on top of the announcer line, at 13 px
findings.detail: The one line that teaches a phone player to move and look shares its slot with the announcer's caption, so the announcer's words show through between the hint's words at the moment a new player is reading it. Both are at the small size, under the 14 px phone minimum. The same collision is in score-lines@phone and range-hud@phone whenever a caption or toast is up, and scoreboard@phone shows the caption half under the board.
findings.fix: On touch, stack the two instead of sharing one slot: hint line at the bottom offset, caption and toast one row above it (or hold captions while a hint is up). Set both to 14 px or more on a phone.
findings.evidence: Hint text 'Move with your left thumb. Drag the right side to look' box [287,290,309,13] at 13 px; caption 'Announcer' [284,294,63,13] and 'Team deathmatch. The range is hot.' [357,294,205,13] at 13 px: same rows, 4 px apart. On desktop the two stand on separate rows (y 877 and y 923) and the hint is 16 px. touch-layout.ts gives .ds-toast, .ds-hintline and .ds-caption the same bottom offset and --ds-type-small. · Hint 'Move with your left thumb. Drag the right side to look' at [287,290,309,13]; toast 'Announcer' [284,294,63,13] + 'Team deathmatch. The range is hot.' [357,294,205,13]: same y within 4 px, x ranges overlap fully. On desktop they stack (toast y 880, hint y 924). Both 13 px; the goal line on the same phone is 16 px. · Hint text box [287,290,309,13] and announcer caption [357,294,205,13] with its label [284,294,63,13] intersect; in the screenshot "Announcer  Team deathmatch. The range is hot." shows through the plate behind "Move with your left thumb. Drag the right side to look". · Hint text box [287,290,309,13]; caption "Announcer" [284,294,63,13] and "Team deathmatch. The range is hot." [357,294,205,13]: 4 px apart vertically, fully overlapping horizontally. Desktop: caption y 877, hint y 923.
alsoNoted: hierarchy: The hint line and the announcer toast are drawn in the same slot, one on top of the other
hud: On the phone the hint line and the announcer toast are drawn on the same line, one through the other
rules: The first-match control hint and the announcer caption are drawn on the same row

findings.title: The phone's first-match hint is set at 13 px and the Announcer toast shows through its plate
findings.detail: The line that teaches a new phone player how to move and look is at the small label size, while the same hint on desktop is 16 px. It is also drawn on top of the Announcer toast, whose text ghosts through behind it, so two sentences share one strip. The 13 px hint also appears on score-lines@phone and range-hud@phone, and scoreboard@phone leaves the toast showing under the panel edge.
findings.fix: Set the hint line and toast at the body step (16 px) on phones and give them separate slots, or hold the toast until the hint has gone.
findings.evidence: match-hud@phone .dom.json: hint 'Move with your left thumb. Drag the right side to look' [287,290,309,13] at 13 px; 'Announcer' [284,294,63,13] and 'Team deathmatch. The range is hot.' [357,294,205,13] at 13 px in the same band. DESIGN.md calls both the hint line and a toast 'one body-size line' (16 px); TYP-01 asks 14 px for phone body text.

findings.title: The red 'ENEMY' ping label is under 2:1 against walls and foliage
findings.detail: A pinged enemy is marked by a red triangle and the word ENEMY in 13 px red directly on the world. Over green siding the word nearly vanishes, and a red/green pair is the worst case for the most common colour-vision deficiencies. The distance under it, in the text colour, measures more than twice as high on the same background.
findings.fix: Put the ping label on a small ink plate the way ally name tags are ('Rook', 'Ember' are on plates), keeping the red for the triangle and the plate's text.
findings.evidence: contrast.md, scoreboard@desktop: 'Enemy' [966,480,47,13] 13 px bold, declared 6.25, measured p50 1.88 / p10 1.68 (shadow only); '54 m' [975,495,28,13] 13 px p50 4.51 / p10 4.21. The mark keeps a triangle and a word, so it is not colour-only. · "Enemy" [966,480,47,13], 13 px bold #ff6159: measured 1.88:1 (p10 1.68) against a declared 6.25; "54 m" 4.51:1. findings.title: A toast and the enemy markers stay up with the scoreboard and show through and under its panel
findings.detail: With the scoreboard open the announcer toast is half hidden under the panel's bottom edge, and three enemy markers ghost through the middle of the tables between the two teams, next to the rows a player is trying to read. DESIGN.md says the feed, toasts and round banner hide while the scoreboard is up; here they do not, and the world markers are not covered either.
findings.fix: Hide toasts, feed and world markers (enemy, ally, ping) while the scoreboard is up, and make the scoreboard panel fully opaque on a phone so nothing from the world reads through the rows.
findings.evidence: Panel bottom edge at y 298; toast plate [286,287,272,30] with 'Your team has taken the lead.' at [374,294,172,13], cut through its text line. 'ENEMY' labels at [397,171,47,13], [407,171,47,13], [413,171,47,13] with '50 m / 55 m / 57 m' under them, visible between the Blue and Orange tables beside the 'Comet' row. · Board bottom at about y 298; toast "Announcer  Your team has taken the lead." at y 294-307 (label [300,294,63,13]) with its upper half hidden. "Enemy" labels at [397,171,47,13], [407,171,47,13], [413,171,47,13] lie inside the board.

findings.title: The Controls legend that names the touch buttons starts under the fold of the phone's pause menu
findings.detail: Pause is the one place that lists every touch glyph with its name, but on a phone the four destinations take the whole screen and the legend's heading is sliced by the bottom edge. A player who pauses to find out what a button does sees Resume, Loadout, Settings and Leave and nothing that says there is a list to scroll to. On desktop the same legend stands in full at the right.
findings.fix: On a phone in landscape, set the Controls legend in the empty right two thirds beside the destination list (as on desktop) so it shows without scrolling.
findings.evidence: 'Controls' heading box [36,387,115,22] in a 390 px tall viewport: 3 px of it are on screen (contrast.md: p10 1.0, warn). The four buttons are 812 px wide rows ending at y 345 while their labels are at most 140 px wide, so the right 600 px of the screen is empty.

findings.title: "Scoreboard in 0:02" counts down to a scoreboard the phone never shows
findings.detail: At match end the phone tells the player a scoreboard is coming, then the line simply turns into "Back to the lobby in..." (end-vote@phone) with no board on screen. The board is only behind the small scoreboard button at the top left, and nothing points to it, so a player waits for something that does not happen and may leave without seeing the final table.
findings.fix: On touch say what will really happen: show "Back to the lobby in 0:10" from the start and make the board reachable from the line itself, e.g. the scoreboard glyph plus "Scoreboard" as a 44 px tappable plate next to it, with the top-left button lit in signal as the one thing to press now.
findings.evidence: end-panel@phone: "Scoreboard in 0:02" [368,215,108,13], 13 px. end-vote@phone: same slot reads "Back to the lobby in 0:05" [351,215,141,13], no board below the panel; Scoreboard button [12,60,44,44] unlit and unlabelled.

findings.title: The range panel leads with 'TTK' over an empty black box, and sits on the Health label
findings.detail: The Practice Range is where a new player goes first, and its one panel opens with an unexplained abbreviation, four dashes and a blank dark rectangle. Its bottom edge also covers the top of the 'Health' label. The setting that hides it is called 'Range overlay' in Settings, with no description either.
findings.fix: Spell it 'Time to kill', caption the canvas 'Recoil: fire to draw it' or hide it until the first shot, and lift the panel 16 px so it clears the Health label. Give 'Range overlay' a one-line description in Settings.

findings.title: The Practice Range stats panel covers the top of the 'Health' label
findings.detail: In the range the TTK and distance panel is stacked straight above the health readout and its bottom edge cuts through the word 'Health', leaving half-height letters. The label is already the weakest text in that corner.
findings.fix: Anchor the range panel 8 px above the health block (bottom at y 956 or less), or move it to the left edge mid-height.

findings.title: Running text in play is 13 px on a phone: hint line, announcer caption and range overlay
findings.detail: The sentences a player has to read while moving are a step smaller on the phone than on desktop, under the 14 px floor for phone body text. The hint line is the one that teaches the controls. Also on match-hud@phone, score-lines@phone and scoreboard@phone (caption).
findings.fix: Keep the hint line and the caption at --ds-type-body (16 px) on the phone, wrapping to two lines if needed, and leave the 13 px step to short labels.
findings.evidence: Hint line [287,290,309,13] at 13 px (16 px on desktop; DESIGN.md says "one body-size line"). Announcer caption 13 px on phone, e.g. scoreboard@phone [374,294,172,13] (16 px on desktop). Range overlay rows 13 px, sentence case.

findings.title: Desktop sliders are 20 px tall targets
findings.detail: Every range slider in settings is a 20 px tall strip, under the 32 px a mouse target should have, so grabbing the thumb takes care, more so for anyone with a tremor or a low-precision pointer. The main menu's Name field is also sampled at 21 px tall.
findings.fix: Give range inputs a 32 px tall hit area on desktop (padding or min-height on the input, track drawn centred) and let a click anywhere in the row's control column move the thumb.
findings.evidence: settings-hud@desktop: 'HUD size' [660,227,284,20], 'Arm length' [660,667,284,20], 'Gap' [660,724,284,20], 'Thickness' [660,781,284,20]. settings-touch@desktop: 'Touch sensitivity' [660,227,284,20]. main-menu@desktop 'Name' input [1643,77,206,21]. MENU-03 asks about 32 px with a mouse; the phone sliders are 44 px.

findings.title: Sentences a player has to read are set at the 13 px small step on desktop
findings.detail: The rule allows text under 14 px only for short uppercase labels, but section descriptions, the pause screen's controls list and the scoreboard's column heads are 13 px in sentence case. They are readable up close and thin from a sofa. Also on pause@desktop, scoreboard@desktop, profile@desktop and bot-lobby@desktop.
findings.fix: Set descriptions and list rows at --ds-type-body (DESIGN.md already asks for a body-size line under a settings section), and either raise --ds-type-small to 14 px or keep it for uppercase labels and key hints only.
findings.evidence: "Health, ammo, the feed, the match bar and the prompts. The crosshair keeps its own size." [76,242,519,13] at 13 px. contrast.md size warnings: settings-hud@desktop 6, pause@desktop 29 (e.g. "Aim down sights" [1432,513,96,13]), scoreboard@desktop 29, profile@desktop 53, bot-lobby@desktop 18.

findings.title: The challenge 'Capture 4 zones' does not say where zones are
findings.detail: No mode on the Bot Match screen is called zones: they belong to Outposts. A new player reading today's challenges cannot tell which mode to pick to earn this one. Same on the phone Profile.
findings.fix: Name the mode in the challenge: 'Capture 4 zones in Outposts'.
findings.evidence: 'Capture 4 zones' 16 px at [73,739,117,16], '+800 XP'. Mode names in bot-lobby: Team deathmatch, Free-for-all, Outposts, Charge, Gun game. GLOSSARY.md: Zone is Outposts' term.

findings.title: A 'Weapon' heading stands over an empty quarter of the screen
findings.detail: The right column opens with a heading and then nothing: no stats, no picture, no description for the highlighted gun, while the tiles on the left carry only a name and 'Auto' or 'Semi'. DESIGN.md asks that a block on the left be answered on the right 'by the picture or the readouts, never by nothing'; here the answer is an empty heading, and the player has no way to compare weapons.
findings.fix: Fill the column with the focused weapon's readouts on open (damage, rate of fire, range, magazine as a readout strip, plus its model or silhouette), defaulting to the equipped weapon so it is never empty; otherwise remove the heading and let the tiles take the width.
findings.evidence: 'Weapon' heading [1444,147,94,22] with no text below it in a column about 420 px wide down to the footer; tiles show a 16 px name and a 13 px fire mode only; focus opens on DONE.

findings.title: On the phone the goal plate and the Use prompt clamp the crosshair from above and below
findings.detail: During the opening countdown the phone's centre column is solid HUD from top to bottom: match bar, mode name, number, a 424 px wide goal plate, the crosshair, a "USE LOADOUT" plate, a toast and the readouts. The two plates leave about 10 px of air either side of the crosshair, so the first look at the map is through a letterbox.
findings.fix: On touch, move the goal line out of the middle (directly under the match bar in place of the "Team deathmatch" label, or into the toast slot above the readouts) and drop the centre "USE LOADOUT" plate: the lit USE button can carry the word, e.g. "Loadout" as a small label beside it.
findings.evidence: Goal plate about y 134-165 (text [225,141,395,16]); crosshair arms about y 174-216; prompt plate about y 227-257 (text [359,233,126,16]); toast at y 286-316; readouts from y 324. Centre box is 338-506 x 156-234.

findings.title: After the countdown the match's goal survives only as 'TDM · 75'
findings.detail: The goal line 'First team to 75 kills, or ahead when the clock runs out' is up for the three seconds of the countdown. A player who missed it finds only the code 'TDM · 75' under the clock, and neither the scoreboard nor the pause screen says what wins. Same on the phone.
findings.fix: Put the goal line in the scoreboard's header beside the mode name ('First team to 75 kills · 10 min'), and write the bar's label as 'First to 75'.
findings.evidence: 'TDM · 75' 13 px at [939,60,48,13]. scoreboard@desktop texts: 'Team deathmatch', '8 players', team names and columns, no goal. pause@desktop: destinations and the Controls legend only.

findings.title: The scoreboard spends a column on Ping that is a dash on every row of a Bot Match
findings.detail: In a Bot Match every seat's ping is "-", so each team table carries a column with no information, on the phone at the cost of name and score width. The "#" column likewise reads 1, 1, 1, 1 until someone scores (scoreboard@desktop). The same dead column is on the desktop board and the end board (end-vote@desktop).
findings.fix: Leave the Ping column out when no seat has a measured ping (offline and bot-only matches) and give its width to the name; show a rank number only once a team's scores differ, or a dash for a tie at zero.
findings.evidence: "Ping" heads at [380,125,26,13] and [724,125,26,13] with 8 of 8 rows showing "-" in scoreboard@phone, scoreboard@desktop and end-vote@desktop; scoreboard@desktop "#" column is "1" on all eight rows.

findings.title: The title and display steps land 2 px apart on a phone, so the page title and the actions read as one size
findings.detail: The scale is meant to have nothing in between, but on a short phone the two fluid steps meet: 'Paused' and 'Resume' are almost the same size and weight, so neither reads as the heading of the other. Same on main-menu@phone ('Duty Shooter' 32 px over 30 px destinations); on desktop the order is the other way round (title 51.84 px, destinations 60 px).
findings.fix: On a phone held sideways drop overlay and page titles to the heading step (22 px), as DESIGN.md already says for the .ds-page header, so the display-size actions are the only large type.
findings.evidence: 'Paused' [16,49,124,32] 32 px bold uppercase; 'Resume' [38,122,120,30] 30 px bold uppercase. main-menu@phone: 32 px vs 30 px. Desktop: 51.84 px vs 60 px.

findings.title: Pause actions are 6 px apart, and the settings tabs 2 px, under the 8 px minimum between touch targets
findings.detail: Resume and Leave are in one tight column, so a thumb landing on a seam can pick the neighbour, and Leave ends the match. The settings tabs on a phone are 44 px tall with 2 px between them (settings@phone, settings-touch@phone, settings-hud@phone). On desktop four sliders are 20 px tall, under the ~32 px mouse minimum.
findings.fix: Raise the pause list's row gap to 8 px, set the tabs' gap to 8 px on touch, and give range inputs and the name field a 44 px (touch) or 32 px (mouse) hit box.
findings.evidence: RESUME [16,111,812,54], LOADOUT [16,171,812,54], SETTINGS [16,231,812,54], LEAVE [16,291,812,54]: 6 px gaps (desktop also 6 px: [56,165,440,73] to [56,244,440,73]). Phone tabs e.g. TOUCH [136,10,69,44] to CONTROLS [207,10,96,44]: 2 px. settings-hud@desktop sliders 284x20 (HUD size [660,227,284,20], Arm length, Gap, Thickness); main-menu Name input 206x21 on all three viewports.

findings.title: "TTK" in the range overlay is never spelled out
findings.detail: The Practice Range is where a new player goes to learn, and its overlay leads with an abbreviation only shooter regulars know. Nothing on the screen or in Settings ("Range overlay") says it means time to kill. Same on range-hud@phone.
findings.fix: Label the row "Time to kill" (it fits the panel's width), or expand it the first time the overlay shows.
findings.evidence: "TTK" [68,733,22,13] on desktop, [78,51,22,13] on phone; no expansion in the overlay, the hint line or the HUD and crosshair settings tab.

findings.title: The phone's hint line and toasts drop to 13 px, the smallest step, for full sentences
findings.detail: The one instruction a new phone player must read while already moving is set smaller than on desktop, on the smaller screen. The announcer toast and the range rows are 13 px too. DESIGN.md specifies the hint line and a toast as body size (16 px).
findings.fix: Keep --ds-type-body (16 px) for the hint line and toasts on the phone and buy the width with shorter copy ("Left thumb moves. Right side looks"), so the plate still ends clear of the Grenade button at x 616.
findings.evidence: "Move with your left thumb. Drag the right side to look" [287,290,309,13] is 13 px (desktop "Move. The mouse looks" is 16 px); announcer caption 13 px on phone vs 16 px on desktop (match-hud); contrast.md marks them size-warn. Rule floor for phone body text is 14 px.
